LLM auditresponse for dotnet.sh:
<security_assessment>
  <decision>SAFE</decision>
  <details>
    The file `dotnet.sh` is a small Bash script meant to configure the dotnet toolchain on Arch Linux. It first checks whether the variables `DOTNET_ROOT` and `DOTNET_TOOLS_PATH` are already defined and exports default values (`/usr/share/dotnet` and `$HOME/.dotnet/tools`) otherwise. Then it updates the `$PATH` by prepending those directories when they are missing. Finally it sets `DOTNET_BUNDLE_EXTRACT_BASE_DIR` using the XDG cache variable, falling back to `$HOME/.cache/dotnet_bundle_extract`. The script performs no network calls, does not run `eval`, `base64`, `curl`, or `wget`, and only modifies local environment variables and PATH entries — a routine behavior for AUR helper scripts.

    Because there is no evidence of data exfiltration, remote code execution, or injection of code from an unexpected host, the package follows ordinary packaging practices. Unpinned sources or missing checksums are hygiene items, not indicators of compromise.
  </details>
  <evidence>
  </evidence>

</security_assessment>
